Celtic won the '''1985–86 Scottish Premier Division''' and became champions in one of the closest finishes in League history. On the final day of the season Hearts were leading Celtic by two points, and a draw against [[Dundee F.C.|Dundee]] would have been sufficient to see them win their first League title since the [[1959–60 in Scottish football|1959–60 season]]. Hearts lost 2–0 to Dundee at [[Dens Park]] thanks to two late goals by [[Substitute (football)|substitute]] [[Albert Kidd]], while Celtic beat St Mirren 5–0 at [[Love Street (stadium)|Love Street]]. As a result, Celtic won the league on goal difference.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Paul |first1=Ian |title=Celtic keep bargain - with a little help from Dundee|date=5 May 1986|work= Glasgow Herald |url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?id=l7ZAAAAAIBAJ&sjid=t6UMAAAAIBAJ&pg=2512%2C1047906 |access-date=15 October 2022}}</ref>

Relegation was suspended due to league reconstruction, therefore Motherwell and Clydebank retained their Premier Division status.

Much of the season was only viewed by fans in stadiums as a dispute between television companies and the [[Scottish Football League]] resulted in no televised Scottish league football between September 1985 and March 1986.<ref>{{cite web|title=Dens memories reduce former Hearts manager to tears - Scotsman.com Sport |url=https://www.scotsman.com/sport/dens-memories-reduce-former-hearts-manager-tears-2475971 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121008043619/http://sport.scotsman.com/heartofmidlothianfc/Dens-memories-reduce-former-Hearts.2751855.jp |archive-date=2012-10-08 |url-status=live |access-date=2009-04-05 }}</ref>
